title: Canonical split top cancellation homotopy
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $B$ an integer-indexed cochain complex of $\mathcal O_S$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. For $m\in\mathbb N$, suppose $B$ is supported in degrees at most $m+1$ and its differential $\delta:B^m\to B^{m+1}$ has a right inverse. The canonical truncation $\tau_{\le m}B$ (cycles in degree $m$, the original terms below $m$, and zero terms above $m$) is chain homotopy equivalent to $B$.

source.place: Tags 068V and 00MT; explicit categorical split identity-pair cancellation expanding the planned argument

proof.text: Take the canonical truncation at m. For a section σ of δ, the endomorphism id - σ∘δ factors through the cycles. This gives the inverse of the canonical inclusion, identity below m and zero above m. The differential-square equation proves the chain-map identities and the kernel equation gives inverse composed with inclusion equal to identity.

The degree-minus-one family consisting of σ from m+1 to m and zero elsewhere contracts the complementary identity pair. Its boundary is σ∘δ in degree m, δ∘σ=id in degree m+1, and zero elsewhere. Above m+1 use the assumed zero terms. This proves the other inverse identity up to homotopy and constructs HomotopyEquiv.
